headline: 17 Ethereum L1 bridge contracts catalogued from official docs; no GitHub repo or audits found; owner of CoreProxyAdmin/L1ProxyAdmin not yet read on-chain.

findings.text: D1: Direct Etherscan fetches blocked (allowlist rejection). Search grounding surfaced the Robinhood Chain Blockscout explorer (robinhoodchain.blockscout.com) as the L2 explorer; Etherscan is used for L1 contracts. No additional name-tagged addresses surfaced beyond what D2 provides. Recorded as unknowns for on-chain confirmation.

D2: Official deployments doc found at https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/protocol-contracts/ — fetched directly. Page lists 17 named Ethereum L1 contracts (Rollup, SequencerInbox, CoreProxyAdmin, DelayedInbox, Bridge, Outbox, L1GatewayRouter, L1ERC20Gateway, L1ArbCustomGateway, L1WethGateway, L1Weth/WETH9, L1ProxyAdmin, L1Multicall) plus L2 bridge contracts. All extracted with roles.
D3: No audit links provided in protocol.audit_links; no audit PDFs surfaced in any fetched or searched source. Recording as unknown.
D4: No GitHub repository provided in protocol.github; no GitHub repo discovered via search. Recording as unknown.

D5: Protocol.chains lists only Ethereum (L1). Robinhood Chain itself (chainId 4663) is the L2 but is not in the DeFiPunkd supported chain list, so L2 contract surfacer URLs cannot be built for this run. L2 bridge contract addresses (L2GatewayRouter, L2ERC20Gateway, L2ArbCustomGateway, L2WethGateway, L2Weth, L2ProxyAdmin) recorded in admin_addresses for completeness with chain='Robinhood Chain (4663)'.

D6: No factory-pattern contracts identified in the bridge address set. L1GatewayRouter and L1ERC20Gateway are routing/escrow contracts, not factories spawning enumerable children. No D6 enumeration required.

D7: Role taxonomy applied. CoreProxyAdmin and L1ProxyAdmin resolve to the same address (0x1232813BDd40aa9d53066A880dE78a4Be70B90FD), classified proxy_admin/unknown actor pending on-chain owner read. Rollup classified as other/unknown. All gateway contracts classified as router or other.
D8: All 17 addresses in admin_addresses trace to the fetched protocol contracts page (https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/protocol-contracts/). No snippet-only sightings without full-page backing.

rationale.verdict: Walked the official Robinhood Chain documentation site (protocol-contracts page fetched directly); catalogued 17 named Ethereum L1 bridge/rollup contracts and 6 L2 token-bridge contracts. No GitHub repo or audit PDFs available to walk. On-chain reads of owner/admin addresses blocked (Etherscan direct fetch rejected, DeFiPunkd surfacer URLs not pre-built). Grade unknown pending on-chain verification of proxy admin ownership and admin role holders.

Support page confirming operator entity is Robinhood Digital Assets LLC (RHDA); developer contact email chain-developers-group@robinhood.com; Stock Tokens are tokenized debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited.

protocol_metadata.about: Robinhood Chain Bridge is the canonical Arbitrum-based bridge connecting Ethereum mainnet to Robinhood Chain (chainId 4663), an Arbitrum Orbit Layer 2 built by Robinhood Digital Assets LLC. Users deposit ETH or ERC-20 tokens via the Delayed Inbox on Ethereum, which creates retryable tickets executed on Robinhood Chain within ~10 minutes; withdrawals follow the standard 7-day Arbitrum challenge period before funds can be claimed on Ethereum. The bridge uses a gateway router architecture (L1/L2 ERC20 Gateway, Custom Gateway, WETH Gateway) and inherits Ethereum security through the Rollup contract and outbox mechanism. Robinhood Chain is purpose-built for tokenized real-world assets and equities, with ETH as the native gas token and first-come-first-served sequencing.
